title: WAN

detail.label: Backup
detail.value: M.2 cellular modem (Quectel EM05-G, WWAN0), or USB phone tethering (Android RNDIS)

notes: Ethernet is the primary internet connection. If it goes down, the router can fail over to cellular through a built-in M.2 LTE modem, or by tethering an Android phone over USB.

title: LAN
notes: Ethernet ports for wired devices on the home network.

title: Wi-Fi

detail.label: Mesh
detail.value: Can act as an EasyMesh controller, extending coverage with extenders

notes: Wi-Fi access point for wireless devices, covering 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands.

title: Bluetooth / IoT

detail.label: Tested with
detail.value: TP-Link Tapo smart plug (Matter over Wi-Fi), onvis smart plug (Matter over Thread)

notes: A multiprotocol radio for connecting smart-home devices over Bluetooth, Zigbee, or Thread. Bluetooth is also used to set up new Matter devices.

title: Packet Processor
notes: Speeds up routing and NAT by handling it in hardware instead of software, so the CPU isn't doing that work for every packet.

title: AI / NPU
notes: Not present on this hardware today. A future board revision could add one as a plug-in module, for on-device AI features.

title: USB

detail.label: Used for
detail.value: Cellular backup modem, Android phone tethering, IoT test devices

notes: A general-purpose USB port, currently used for the cellular backup connection and for connecting IoT devices during testing.

title: SIM Card Slot
notes: Holds the SIM for the cellular backup modem.

title: Storage
notes: Onboard flash storage for the firmware, with A/B partitions so updates can be applied safely.

title: SD Card Slot
notes: A removable SD card slot, tested and working on this hardware.

title: Media Tuner
notes: No tuner hardware on this profile — it connects over Ethernet, not cable, DSL, or fiber.

title: Debug Port
notes: A serial console and JTAG access for low-level debugging during development.

title: WPS Button
notes: A physical button for quick Wi-Fi setup, so a new device can join without typing a password.

title: Reset Button
notes: A physical button to restore the router to its factory default settings.

title: Power Button
notes: A physical power switch for the device.
